# Baseline model evaluation report (auto-generated by scripts/evaluate_baseline.py)

**Read first.** Labels are automatic (rules + Claude's reading, label policy v2), **not** independently human-verified. `test_hindi` / `test_hinglish` come from LLM-generated Dataset D and are awaiting independent review; the 45-message benchmark is too small for stable estimates. This is a pipeline-verification baseline, not a final model. Do not quote these numbers as real-world performance.

## Training setup
- train: 52966 messages (15683 scam = 29.6%, 37283 legitimate); class weights from train only: legitimate 0.71, scam 1.69
- features: char_wb 2-5-grams (<=300k) + word 1-2-grams (<=150k), TF-IDF fitted on train only; logistic regression C=4 (liblinear), seed 42
- thresholds chosen on validation only: F1-optimal = 0.584; max-recall at precision>=95% = 0.528; default = 0.500

### 95% bootstrap intervals at the validation-chosen F1 threshold (matter most for the small sets)

| set                         | F1 95% CI   | PR-AUC 95% CI   |
|:----------------------------|:------------|:----------------|
| validation                  | 0.96-0.97   | 0.99-0.99       |
| test (main, mostly English) | 0.97-0.97   | 0.99-0.99       |
| test_hindi                  | 0.72-0.87   | 0.81-0.94       |
| test_hinglish               | 0.83-0.90   | 0.95-0.98       |
| benchmark (45, curated)     | 0.84-0.97   | 0.94-1.00       |

> `majority_accuracy` is the accuracy of predicting 'legitimate' for everything; accuracy alone is not a valid measure here.

**test_hindi:** F1 0.80, precision 0.79, recall 0.81 on 146 messages (74 scams); CI width shows how little a set this small can say.

**test_hinglish:** F1 0.87, precision 0.82, recall 0.92 on 299 messages (156 scams); CI width shows how little a set this small can say.
